newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB Swiss shares fall on results.
newsitem.headline: ABB Swiss shares fall on results.

text.p: Swiss-listed shares in ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG lost ground in an otherwsie stronger market after publishing 1996 results on Thursday.
Bearer shares in ABB AG, a Swiss holding company that has 50 percent of the ABB group, were down around 70 Swiss francs or 3.9 percent at 1,740 about an hour after the Swiss Exchange opened.
Traders said the 1996 group results were below expectations. ABB, whose other half is held by Sweden's ABB AB, saw group net profit fall 6.2 percent to $1.233 billion from $1.315 billion in 1995.

A Reuters survey of ten analysts in Zurich, London and Stockholm before the ABB release had shown an average expected profit of $1.30 billion, down 1.1 percent. 1995 was boosted by a one-off gain of 250 million dollar from the Adtraz transportation venture with Daimler-Benz.
The poll's range was between 1.245 and 1.36 billion.
Analyst Paolo Orler at Zurich Cantonal Bank said analysts would now likely reduce their 1997 profit estimates for ABB.
Orler, who had forecast net profit at $1.34 billion, said market expectations had been higher in part due to general optimism om Swiss and other equity markets.
